Method of Attack: Encrypts portions of the hard drive including the Master Boot Record (MBR) and Master File Table (MFT), rendering the system unbootable and files inaccessible
Replaces the boot drive's MBR with a malicious loader that pretends to run CHKDSK while encrypting the MFT
Displays a lock screen demanding ransom payment in bitcoins via a TOR site
Distributed via emails targeting human resources departments with Dropbox links to malicious installers
Attack Vector: Phishing emails with Dropbox links to malicious executable files
Indicators of Compromise: Lock screen with instructions to connect to a TOR site and unique ID
